architecture_summary: url-pulse is a single-process Express HTTP server backed by a local SQLite database. Incoming requests are routed to thin route handlers that delegate to a Check Service (for POST /check) or a History Service (for GET /history*). A shared Database layer encapsulates all SQLite access via better-sqlite3. There are no background processes, queues, or external services.

components.name: HTTP Server
components.purpose: Bootstrap the Express application, register middleware (JSON body parsing, error handling), mount all routes, and start listening on a configured port.
responsibilities: Initialize the Express app instance.
Register JSON body-parser middleware.
Mount route definitions from Check and History handlers.
Register a global error-handling middleware.
Start the HTTP server and bind to the configured port.

components.name: Check Handler
components.purpose: Handle POST /check: validate the incoming URL, perform an outbound HTTP GET with high-resolution timing, persist the result via the Database layer, and return the status code and response time to the caller.
responsibilities: Validate that the request body contains a non-empty, well-formed URL.
Record a start timestamp using a high-resolution timer.
Perform an outbound HTTP GET request to the provided URL.
Record elapsed time in milliseconds upon response or error.
Delegate persistence of the check record to the Database layer.
Return a JSON response containing status_code and response_time_ms.
Handle network errors and timeouts gracefully without crashing.

components.name: History Handler
components.purpose: Handle GET /history and GET /history/:id: retrieve check records from the Database layer and return them as JSON, returning 404 when a requested record does not exist.
responsibilities: Handle GET /history by querying all check records from the Database layer and returning them as a JSON array.
Handle GET /history/:id by querying a single check record by integer ID from the Database layer.
Return HTTP 404 with an error message when the requested ID does not exist.
Return HTTP 400 when the :id path parameter is not a valid integer.

components.name: Database Layer
components.purpose: Encapsulate all SQLite interactions via better-sqlite3: initialize the database file and schema on startup, and provide synchronous insert and query operations for check records.
responsibilities: Open or create the SQLite database file at a configured path.
Create the checks table if it does not already exist (id, url, status_code, response_time_ms, error, checked_at).
Provide a synchronous insertCheck function that persists a new check record and returns the generated id.
Provide a synchronous getAllChecks function that returns all records ordered by checked_at descending.
Provide a synchronous getCheckById function that returns a single record by integer id, or null if not found.

data_flows.description: HTTP Server routes POST /check requests to the Check Handler.
HTTP Server routes GET /history and GET /history/:id requests to the History Handler.
Check Handler calls insertCheck on the Database Layer to persist a completed check record (url, status_code, response_time_ms, error).
History Handler calls getAllChecks or getCheckById on the Database Layer to retrieve stored records.
Database Layer returns the generated record id to the Check Handler after insert.
Database Layer returns check record(s) or null to the History Handler.

open_design_questions: [DESIGN_DECISION] Should the SQLite database file path default to ./data/checks.db and be overridable via a DATABASE_PATH environment variable?
[DESIGN_DECISION] Should the server port default to 3000 and be overridable via a PORT environment variable?
[DESIGN_DECISION] Should POST /check follow HTTP redirects automatically, and what should the maximum redirect count be (suggested default: follow up to 5)?
[DESIGN_DECISION] What should the default outbound HTTP request timeout be for POST /check (suggested: 10 seconds)?
[CLARIFICATION] Should GET /history support any ordering or filtering options, or is reverse-chronological order sufficient for this iteration?
